faq.question: Who is wovain for?
faq.answer: Independent designers and small labels who sell graphic pieces through print-on-demand: tees, sweatshirts, totes and prints on Fourthwall.

faq.question: Will it make my label look generic?
faq.answer: You set the direction and approve every piece. Reject a design with a note and wovain draws another round. Nothing is listed without your yes.

faq.question: Will wovain spend money on ads by itself?
faq.answer: No. Every campaign is created paused, at the daily budget you choose, from $1 to $500. Spend starts only when you turn it on in Meta Ads Manager.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: A Fourthwall shop for the products, a fal account for the artwork and a Meta ad account for the campaign. You connect each one with its own sign-in after you create your account.

faq.question: Will my shop be ready to sell?
faq.answer: Yes. The Store lists what your Fourthwall shop needs before it can take an order (payouts, shipping, going live, the Meta pixel), does what it can for you and links to the rest, then ticks each step off by itself. It also rewrites each product page the way an e-commerce copywriter would, and nothing changes until you approve it.

faq.question: How are prices set?
faq.answer: From the blank's real base cost on Fourthwall: at least $10 profit and a 30% margin, after card fees, sales tax and a refund reserve, rounded up to a whole dollar. When you change a price, wovain shows your profit in every size against Fourthwall's real cost and refuses one that loses money.

faq.question: What does it cost?
faq.answer: wovain's plans are on the pricing page. Production is paid from each sale through Fourthwall, artwork is billed by fal and ad spend by Meta, each to your own account.

faq.question: Can I use it in ChatGPT?
faq.answer: Yes. wovain is also an app in ChatGPT, with the same steps and approvals. The docs explain how to add it.

faq.question: Who owns the designs?
faq.answer: You own your briefs and the designs you approve. wovain screens drafts for names and trademarks, but you stay responsible for what you publish.

faq.question: Who sees my ads?
faq.answer: People who love what your label loves. Qloo picks that audience from the brands in your profile, and every ad is written for them. If wovain can't find that audience, it makes no ads and tells you what to add.

faq.question: What stops my ads from losing money?
faq.answer: wovain checks your ads every 30 minutes. It pauses an ad that spends one sale's profit without a sale, and pauses all spend at your daily cap, your monthly cap or your loss limit ($50 unless you change it). It asks before it raises the budget of a winner. You get an alert each time, by email, on your phone or on Telegram.

faq.question: Which of my designs should I advertise?
faq.answer: All of them, at first. wovain tests up to five designs in one campaign, gives each a fair share of the budget, pauses the ones that lose money and shows you the winner, so the budget follows the design that sells.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: We keep as little as we can, and we never sell data.
privacy.collectBody: Your name, email and password hash for your account; the briefs you write; and the drops, designs and products wovain makes for you.
privacy.analyticsBody: We use PostHog, hosted in the US, to learn how people find and use wovain: the pages you visit, what you click, page speed, the site's language and your country. Your country comes from your IP address, which isn't kept, and the page checks whether an automated browser is driving it, so bots aren't counted as visitors. Until you accept, it runs without cookies or browser storage, so it can't recognize you across visits or record replays. If you accept, or where the law doesn't require asking first, it stores an ID in your browser and records session replays, with everything you type and your account details hidden. You can change your choice at any time with Cookie settings at the bottom of the page, and a Global Privacy Control signal from your browser counts as a no. Once you sign in, these events are tied to your account's id, never your email.
privacy.connectionsBody: When you connect Fourthwall, Meta or fal, we store the access they grant so wovain can act for you. You can disconnect any of them at any time from Connections.
privacy.processorsBody: Briefs and designs are sent to the services that do the work: Nebius, Qloo, Tavily, fal, Fourthwall and Meta. Each handles data under its own policy.
privacy.voiceBody: When you hold the microphone button, fal turns your recording into text, and Nebius reads the text so wovain can work out what you asked. wovain doesn't store the recording or the text. fal and Nebius handle them under their own terms. Analytics only records which kind of command it was, never what you said.
privacy.deleteBody: Email {privacyEmail} from your account's address and we delete your account, drops and stored connections within 30 days.

Pricing.lead: Start free with {credits, number} credits every month. Studio, Label and credit packs are coming soon. wovain never takes a cut of your sales.

Pricing.yoursTitle: What you pay on your own accounts
Pricing.yoursLead: Credits cover wovain's work: trend research, briefs, design checks and ad copy. The rest you pay directly, on accounts you own, with no markup from wovain.

fal.name: fal
fal.body: Artwork is drawn on your fal account and billed by fal per image.

meta.name: Meta
meta.body: Ad spend, billed by Meta to your ad account, and only after you turn a paused campaign on.

fourthwall.name: Fourthwall
fourthwall.body: Blanks and printing, paid out of each sale. Nothing to buy up front.

credit.question: What is a credit?
credit.answer: A credit pays for one unit of wovain's work. Trend research takes 5, a design takes 4, and ad copy or an autopilot call takes 1, and each drop draws three designs, so a drop you approve step by step is about 18 credits. If a step fails, its credits come back.

yours.question: What do I pay outside wovain?
yours.answer: Art, ads and products run on your own accounts. fal bills you for the artwork, Meta bills your ad account once you start a campaign, and Fourthwall takes the blank's cost out of each sale.

cancel.question: Can I cancel?
cancel.answer: Yes, any time, from Manage billing. Your plan and its credits stay until the end of the month you paid for, then you're back on Free.

rollover.question: Do unused credits roll over?
rollover.answer: On Free, credits refresh each month and unused ones don't carry over. When Label opens, its unused credits will roll over, and credit packs won't expire.

free.question: What happens when I run out?
free.answer: wovain stops before the step and tells you. Your {freeCredits, number} free credits come back next month, and nothing you made is lost. Paid plans and packs of {packCredits, number} credits are coming soon.

paid.question: When can I buy Studio, Label or credits?
paid.answer: Soon. For now every account is on Free. Press Notify me on the plan you want, so we know which one to open first.

connect.label: Shop connected
connect.done: Connected as the shop's owner or a manager.
connect.todo: wovain needs an owner or manager to run the shop.

payouts.label: Payouts set up
payouts.todo: Fourthwall pays your sales out through Stripe. Setting it up takes about 5 minutes, and only the shop owner can do it.
payouts.waiting: Fourthwall is finishing your payout account.
payouts.inProgress: Stripe still needs a few details before it can pay you.
payouts.step1: Open Billing and payouts in Fourthwall.
payouts.step2: Under How you get paid, choose Set up your payouts.
payouts.step3: Give Stripe your ID and bank details, then come back here. This step ticks off by itself.
payouts.noStripe: Stripe isn't available in your country? Fourthwall pays through PayPal or bill.com instead: once your balance reaches $25, email support@fourthwall.com with your shop's address. When they've set it up, mark this step done.
payouts.markDone: Fourthwall support set up my payouts
payouts.confirmed: You marked payouts as set up by Fourthwall support (PayPal or bill.com).

site_live.label: Shop is live
site_live.todo: Your shop is coming soon. wovain can take it live once you confirm.
site_live.waiting: Fourthwall is reviewing your shop. Only Fourthwall support can finish it.

shipping.label: Shipping is on
shipping.done: Buyers can check out with shipping.
shipping.todo: Turn on shipping and add a shipping profile in Fourthwall. This ticks off here once it's done.

pixel.label: Meta pixel on your shop
pixel.done: Your Meta pixel sees visits and sales from your shop.
pixel.todo: Add your Meta pixel in Fourthwall's settings, then open your storefront once to send a test visit. This ticks off when Meta sees it.
pixel.waiting: Connect Meta first: wovain finds your pixel there.
pixel.noDataset: Meta is connected, but wovain didn't find exactly one pixel on your ad account. Create or pick one in Meta setup.
pixel.step2: In Tracking pixels, paste it into the Facebook Pixel field and save.
pixel.step3: Open your storefront once. This step ticks off when Meta sees the visit, which can take a few minutes.
pixel.capi: To count the sales ad blockers hide, also connect Meta's Conversions API in Fourthwall. It asks for the same pixel ID and an access token from Meta Events Manager.

domain.label: Custom domain
domain.todo: Fourthwall is still verifying your domain's DNS records.
domain.check: Your shop sells on its Fourthwall address. A custom domain is optional.
domain.pending: {domain}: {count, plural, one {# DNS record} other {# DNS records}} not verified yet.

policies.label: Returns, shipping and privacy policies
policies.check: Fourthwall adds default policies. Review them so they match how you sell.

metaSetup.title: Get your Meta account ready for ads
metaSetup.titleReady: Your Meta account is ready for ads
metaSetup.notConnected: Connect your Meta account, and wovain checks what it still needs before your ads can run.
metaSetup.expired: Meta's sign-in expired. Reconnect Meta to see where your account stands.

ad_account.label: Ad account
ad_account.done: Your ad account is open to wovain.
ad_account.todo: You need an ad account. Open Meta's ad accounts page, choose Add, then Create a new ad account. Come back here: this card ticks off by itself.
ad_account.waiting: Meta has restricted this ad account. Open Account quality to see why and what Meta asks for.
ad_account.check: Check your ad account in Meta.

payment.label: Payment method
payment.done: Your ad account has a payment method. Meta bills your ad spend to it.
payment.todo: Meta charges ad spend to a card or PayPal on your ad account. Open Meta's payment settings, choose Add payment method and save it. Come back here: this card ticks off by itself.
payment.waiting: Meta is reviewing this ad account, so payments wait. Open Account quality to see what Meta needs.
payment.check: Check the payment method in Meta.

page.label: Facebook Page
page.done: Your ads run under your Facebook Page.
page.todo: Ads run under a Facebook Page. If you have one, open Pages in Meta's business settings, choose Add and pick it. If not, create one first (a name and a photo are enough). Come back here: this card ticks off by itself.
page.waiting: Set up your ad account first.

instagram.label: Instagram account
instagram.done: Your ads can also run under your Instagram account.
instagram.todo: Optional: link your Instagram account so your ads show your name on Instagram too. Open Instagram accounts in Meta's business settings and choose Add.
instagram.waiting: Set up your ad account first.
instagram.check: Optional: Meta didn't say whether an Instagram account is linked. You can check in Meta's business settings.

safety_rules.label: Safety rules
safety_rules.done: Ready. wovain can set up the rules that pause your ads, even when wovain is offline.
safety_rules.todo: Reconnect Meta and allow everything Meta asks for, so wovain can set up the rules that pause your ads. While Meta reviews wovain's app, this works only for accounts Meta lets test it.
safety_rules.waiting: Available once your ad account is set up.
safety_rules.check: Reconnect Meta to check the safety rules.
